Quadratic Roots

AlgebraCurvesNumber Theory
Game: Build a bent line from three numbers and watch where a circle crosses the bottom line. Those crossing points are the answers to a quadratic equation. There is nothing to win — explore the equation.
How to play: Move the a, b and c sliders to change the equation. Tick names or hint to see more of the construction; press Reset for the starting equation.

Look for the math

A quadratic equation has at most two answers. Instead of a formula, you can draw them: make a bent line out of the three coefficients, draw one circle, and see where it cuts the axis.

A broken line from the coefficients

Put B at the origin. Walk straight up by a to A, back down to B, then walk b along the axis to C, and finally c up or down to D. Negative numbers simply send you the other way. So A is (0, a), C is (b, 0) and D is (b, c).

The circle on AD

Draw the circle whose diameter is AD. Where it cuts the axis at X, the angle AXD is a right angle by Thales' theorem. That turns into x² − bx + ac = 0 for the horizontal position x of X. Tick "Show hint" to see the helper line and "Show names" to see the labelled points.

Where the equation comes from

The starting number a is the unit along the bent line: write x = a·t. Substituting gives a·t² − bt + c = 0 after dividing by a. The applet (following Adler's diagram) therefore solves ax² − bx + c = 0 — note the minus sign before b, not the plus sign in the familiar quadratic equation. With a = 1, b = 5, c = 6 the marked roots are 2 and 3, not −2 and −3. The logic test checks this sign convention on a grid of coefficients.

One root, or none

The discriminant b² − 4ac decides how many green points you see: two when it is positive, one when it is zero (the circle just touches the axis), and none when it is negative. When a = 0 the equation is not quadratic at all: there is one root, c / b. Two roots always add to b / a and multiply to c / a, as Viète's formulas say.

What was checked

The test runs 343 coefficient triples, including negatives, zero and fractions. It checks that E really lies on AD and on the axis, that EF is perpendicular to AD, that the marked points sit on the circle and solve the equation, and that the roots match an independent quadratic formula and Viète's relations. It also confirms the sign swap and the zero-discriminant and a = 0 cases.

Set a = 1 and c = 1, then slide b from −4 to 4 and watch the two green points meet and vanish.
